newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australis says merger talks continue.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australis says merger talks continue.

text.p: Pay tv operator Australis Media Ltd said on Friday it was continuing talks with rival Foxtel about industry rationalisation, which could include a merger.
The company, whose stock was suspended by the Australian Stock Exchange after the end of Thursday trade, said it could not explain hectic trade in its stock on Thursday.
It added that it now had more than 110,000 subscribers, which compares with the 180,000-200,000 subscriber base of its rivals Optus Vision and Foxtel.

"As previously advised to the market, Australis remains in discussions with third parties (in particular Foxtel, News and Telstra) with respect to the possibility of commencing steps towards the rationalisation of components of the Australian pay television industry including the possibility of a merger,' Australis said in a statement to the stock exchange.
"Australis is presently unable to predict whether and, if so, how and when any such rationalisation may occur."
The Australian Financial Review newspaper said on Friday that Foxtel partners News Corp Ltd and Telstra would next week say they had taken a 65 percent stake in Australis.

The deal, which represented a back-door listing for Foxtel, was expected to be ratified by the Australis board on Friday, the paper said. Kerry Packer's Publishing and Broadcasting Ltd is a key shareholder in Australis and one of its major financial backers.
Speculation of a merger heightened on June 20 when PBL and the Foxtel partners said they were working towards the rationalisation of the industry "for the benefit of Foxtel".
Australis shares ended at 20 cents on Thursday, a rise of 5.5 cents, and traded at a high of 25.3 cents on Friday after the ASX suspension was lifted. -- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
